records.title: Photolithography Overlay Map Generation with Implicit Knowledge Distillation Diffusion Transformer

code_evidence_basis.C0: Main methods do not establish embedded governing process physics.
code_evidence_basis.V3: Author-reported measurement-linked overlay comparison; main p7 plus prior targeted supplement EVM audit. Not independent local verification.
code_evidence_basis.M3: Author-reported pilot/process comparison; no independent external-site transfer or operational qualification.

generation.inputs: previous-layer overlay maps, equipment logs and equipment/chuck/reticle IDs
generation.conditioning: multimodal unified contrastive embeddings and gated cross-attention in latent teacher-student diffusion
generation.output_scope: process-linked map images; numerical calibrated overlay vectors are not acquired in this reading batch

claims.paraphrase: IKDDiT conditions current-layer map generation on prior-layer maps, logs and equipment/chuck/reticle identifiers. Masked student and unmasked teacher tokens are aligned with contrastive and discriminator objectives; the decoder denoises visible tokens and reconstructs hidden ones.

Diffusion probability-flow ODEs, feature alignment and equipment conditions do not establish embedded lithography optics/resist equations or calibrated physical constraints. C0 can coexist with measurement-linked industrial evaluation.

MPOM is described as real semiconductor-industry multimodal data: overlay images, logs with 5,781 unique tokens and 152GB total, plus categorical equipment IDs. Image resolution is 512 pixels, batch size 64 and student mask ratio 0.5. Model S/B/XL counts are 19.4/81.6/417.9 million parameters.

The authors compare FID over training iterations. IKDDiT reaches 11.6 at 250k iterations, while DiT/MDT/MaskDiT report 14.1/12.2/11.9 at 500k. This is convergence by iteration count, not measured wall-clock speed or generation throughput.

Pilot-run wafers undergo overlay measurement and APC estimation for a lot of 25 wafers. Reported OME rates are pilot run 6.8%, GAGAN 9.2% and IKDDiT-G 3.2%. Table 4 explicitly states lot size and scanner loss are estimated through simulation: IKDDiT-G 24.1 and 2.3%.

claims.location: Section 4.6; Figures 7-8; prior targeted supplement audit
claims.paraphrase: Figure 7 ground truth is attributed to actual pilot-run data. A prior dated targeted audit separately records the supplement EVM as metrology-derived actual-minus-predicted overlay vectors. This supports provisional paper-reported V3/M3 evidence, not newly completed supplement reading, independent measurement replication or field qualification.

Section 4.1 says training is capped at 1,000 iterations; Sections 4.2-4.4 use 578.1k updates and Section 4.7 says 150k for ablations whose tables are labelled FID-15k. Mask prose on page 5 calls m=1 unmasked while the losses use 1-m for score estimation and m for masked reconstruction. Clarify timestep/update/evaluation-sample definitions and mask conventions against pinned code rather than silently repair them.

Prose says CFG recall ranks second behind MDT-G, whereas Table 3 lists IKDDiT-G recall 0.67 and MDT-G 0.63. Preserve the table and prose separately pending clarification; no locally reproduced ranking is claimed.

author_numeric_results.table_4_lot_size_and_scanner_loss: explicitly estimated through simulation; not observed production KPIs
author_numeric_results.table_4_rework_measurement_provenance: not independently established; caption specifically labels lot size/scanner loss as simulated
author_numeric_results.ablation_table_metric_label: FID-15k; clarify relationship to stated 150k training updates

design_limitations.issue: Main PDF does not establish exact wafer/lot/tool/time split, OME denominator, metrology uncertainty or external holdout. Process evidence must not be erased, but independent qualification remains open.
Lot-size and scanner-loss estimates are explicitly simulated. Rework measurement provenance is not independently established; do not label all columns measured or all columns simulated.
Iteration convergence and GFLOPs are not end-to-end wall-clock or resource measurements.
Keep schedule, mask convention and recall text/table questions separate from proven implementation failures.
Appendix G/I and the metrology definition require separately recorded supplement review, not inferred full coverage.

open_questions: Acquire a lawful MPOM endpoint, checksum, metrology vector representation and task checkpoint.
Fully review the separate supplement and resolve OME/EVM definitions, uncertainty and lot/tool/time independence.
Clarify diffusion timesteps versus training updates, FID-15k labels and mask conventions against immutable code.
Evaluate a named overlay-control use profile with independent metrology and measured production outcomes.

records.title: SeaS: Few-shot Industrial Anomaly Image Generation with Separation and Sharing Fine-tuning

code_evidence_basis.C0: Visual token/image objectives without process laws.
code_evidence_basis.V0: No calibrated process/metrology validation in reviewed main PDF; image/downstream metrics exist separately.

generation.target: normal RGB images and anomalous RGB image-mask pairs
generation.inputs: 60 normal images and one-third masked anomaly images per anomaly type for fine-tuning; a selected normal training image plus noise for inference
generation.conditioning: one normal token and multiple learned anomaly tokens, DA/NA alignment and a separately learned RMP mask branch
generation.output_scope: one generator per product covering its anomaly types; downstream supervised segmenter is shared across products; 3D-AD uses RGB only

claims.paraphrase: SeaS fine-tunes shared product-level U-Net and normal/anomaly tokens using separated DA/NA objectives. RMP combines U-Net and VAE features with real-mask focal supervision. Inference begins from a noised normal training image and averages masks from the final three denoising steps.

claims.location: Mixed training; Section 4.1; supervised segmentation paragraph
claims.paraphrase: One generative model is trained per product across its anomaly types, using 60 normal images and one-third masked anomaly images per type. It produces 1,000 anomaly image-mask pairs per type. The downstream supervised segmentation model is instead shared across all products.
Experiments cover 15 MVTec AD, 12 VisA and 10 MVTec 3D AD categories. MVTec 3D AD is explicitly used for RGB images only, without establishing generated 3D geometry or depth.

IS/IC-LPIPS assess anomalous images, KID assesses normal images, and IC-LPIPS(a) assesses anomaly regions. SeaS reports MVTec/VisA/3D-AD KID values 0.04/0.02/0.06 for normal-image generation, not defect-image KID.

The three downstream uses differ: replace pseudo-anomalies for synthesis-based detectors, add normal images to unsupervised training, and train supervised segmentation from generated pairs plus original normal images. Reported headline gains are +8.66 pixel AP, +1.10 image AP and +12.79 IoU with percent labels; do not pool these unlike tasks.

Table 2 DRAEM MVTec IoU decreases 60.30 to 58.87 after SeaS; GLASS VisA pixel AUROC decreases 98.47 to 98.43. Table 3 MambaAD MVTec 3D AD pixel AP decreases 37.30 to 35.46. Retain adverse cells alongside headline averages.

Learned image/token alignment and mask refinement do not establish physically manufacturable novel defects or independent metrology. Recombination examples support visual diversity claims, not a process-physics acceptance test. Offline RGB benchmarks support C0/V0/M2.

F1-max is reported at an optimal threshold; operational threshold calibration and acceptance must be separately evaluated. Exact training, mask threshold and other ablations are deferred to appendix A, which is not completely read in this batch.

design_limitations.issue: Product-level generator sharing differs from all-products segmentation sharing; preserve both scopes.
Inference uses a source normal image. Preserve source-image lineage rather than count all output variation as unconditional new examples.
KID is for normal images; 3D-AD contains RGB-only experiments. Dataset or metric names do not establish different output modalities.
Multiple adverse metric cells remain despite improving averages; no all-metric/all-regime gain is established.
Optimal-threshold F1 and remaining-image tests are not independent factory acceptance. Separate appendix and split provenance remain open.

open_questions: Fully read appendix A and record split/image lineage, thresholding and repeated-seed definitions.
Acquire pinned product-level generator and RMP weights, separate from generated output archives.
Evaluate source-image memorization, mask semantic validity and adverse metric cells with independent validators.
Measure generation-plus-mask resource cost and qualify an external manufacturing use profile.

records.title: Training-Free Industrial Defect Generation with Diffusion Models

code_evidence_basis.C0: Inference feature/image constraints without governing process physics.
code_evidence_basis.V0: No calibrated process/metrology validation in reviewed main PDF; visual/downstream scores recorded separately.

generation.target: defective RGB images on source normal backgrounds with supplied target masks
generation.inputs: normal background, reference defect image/mask and augmented real target mask placed within a predefined affected-object area
generation.conditioning: AnyDoor/DINOv2/ControlNet plus inference-time Sinkhorn feature alignment, adaptive mask and texture guidance
generation.resolution_reported: not established as a uniform output resolution in reviewed main PDF
generation.output_scope: mask-conditioned image editing; target-mask annotations are supplied, not independently measured output ground truth

claims.paraphrase: TF-IDG avoids task-specific model retraining but performs gradient-guided latent optimization using reference defects. DDIM inversion stores reference/background features; Sinkhorn alignment and adaptive masks guide early sampling, followed by attention/AdaIN texture preservation.

Inputs include a normal background, reference defect image with mask and a target generation mask. Augmented real masks are randomly placed within a predefined affected-object region; supplied mask placement remains an input/provenance requirement.

Few-shot uses one-third of each defect category as reference and remaining two-thirds as test. One-shot uses one reference anomaly per category. Sampling uses AnyDoor-trained SD2.1/ControlNet, DINOv2 guidance 4.5, 50 steps, Tn=30, Ti=25 and eta=0.04. Reported output count is 1,000 image-mask pairs per anomaly type.

Local IS is computed on mask-cropped defect regions, unlike whole-image IS in SeaS. TF-IDG reports MVTec/VisA Local IS 3.32/3.90 and IC-LPIPS 0.32/0.30; the latter ties displayed AnoDiff/AnoGen values rather than uniformly exceeding them.

Classification Table 2 lists 14 categories with mean accuracy 79.84% few-shot and 71.92% one-shot. Grid accuracy is 40.00% few-shot versus DIAG 46.74% and AnoDiff 42.50%; the one-shot grid value is 31.58%. Preserve exceptions alongside mean improvements.

The paper evaluates generated-data UNet localization/detection and ResNet-34 classification, plus replacement of GLASS synthesis and augmentation of UniAD anomaly features. These are distinct downstream regimes rather than one pooled comparison.

The main metric paragraph defines Pro as area under the precision-recall curve while also reporting AP. Resolve the exact implementation before equating it with other papers' PRO. Table 5 displayed VisA GLASS Pro values are 92.2 to 95.3 while prose says 3.4% improvement; preserve the displayed values and prose separately.

The authors explicitly note that one-shot may bias the learned distribution toward the reference defect and harm generalization. More seen examples improve aggregate scores, but unseen defect/factory coverage is not independently qualified.

Sinkhorn feature distances, pixel differences and texture matching are visual constraints, not independent process residuals or calibrated defect morphology. Training-free removes task fine-tuning but not pretrained asset, inversion, memory-bank, gradient or mask-preparation costs. Offline benchmarks support C0/V0/M2.

author_numeric_results.Pro_printed_definition: Area Under the Precision-Recall curve; exact implementation unresolved before cross-paper PRO equivalence

design_limitations.issue: Training-free still incurs inversion, feature-bank, mask preparation and gradient-guided inference cost; no new timing measurement exists.
Reference defect/mask, background and target affected-object region require explicit provenance and semantic acceptance.
Local IS and whole-image IS are not the same estimand; IC-LPIPS has displayed ties.
Classification Table 2 has 14 categories, not 15. Grid performance does not exceed all comparators.
Resolve Pro definition and text-versus-table gain interpretation before metric normalization; do not silently overwrite values.
One-shot reference bias is an author-acknowledged limitation; no external-site/process acceptance follows from benchmark averages.

open_questions: Fully read separate supplement and resolve Pro code, mask handling, split provenance and seed definitions.
Acquire all attributable pretrained assets and verify rights/checksums, including bundled iseg dependency.
Measure cold-start inference including DDIM inversion, gradients and mask preparation under a declared budget.
Independently validate supplied-mask/defect correspondence and per-category harms before any external industrial profile pass.
